title: Arts funding review deferred pending municipal input
subtitle: Also: provincial offences court space needs and the first-quarter 2025 plan and financial update.
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee spent most of its meeting on the Region's Arts Funding Governance Review. Staff proposed hiring an outside community partner to run the arts fund for three years and exploring an arts council. The committee instead voted to defer the item {{vote:m5}}. Staff are to report back to Council on June 25 on running the 2025 funding in-house, and the broader recommendations are to return in the fall after area municipalities have had a say.

This matters to residents because the arts fund is one of the few programs open to individual artists, and the committee's debate centred on keeping 2025 funding flowing while giving cities and townships a voice. Council makes the final decision.

On the consent agenda, the committee recommended receiving the first-quarter 2025 plan and financial update and amending the capital budget and forecast {{vote:m3}}. It also received a report on Provincial Offences Court needs for information. The report describes growing caseloads and cramped facilities, and staff plan a report in the fall that includes rental options. The next meeting is August 12.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended deferring the item, with staff to report to Council on June 25 on running 2025 arts funding in-house and the remaining recommendations, including an arts council, to return in fall 2025 after consulting area municipalities.
The committee recommended that Council receive the first-quarter update on the 2025 business plan and amend the 2025 Capital Budget and 2026-2034 Capital Forecast as set out in Appendix B.

debate: One councillor said the consultant did not engage area municipal staff, even though the changes could affect city arts budgets. The councillor also raised concern about the Region taking on work that has historically been municipal. Staff replied that municipal arts managers were kept informed through a working group and would be fully involved in long-term options.

Staff said the Region lacks the capacity to run the fund in-house, citing a large time commitment and the need for an outside jury. They also said the community foundation that ran it last year has declined to continue. Some councillors asked whether staff could do it for one year anyway.

Several councillors supported exploring an arts council, partly to reduce the political element in arts funding. Others said politics cannot be removed and that Council should keep some control over outcomes. One councillor questioned why an arts council would take three years.

One councillor raised concern that Cambridge and the townships have received little of the funding. Staff said geographic distribution could be written into the contract terms and that outreach to those areas is needed.

On the court report, a councillor questioned the space estimates and the forecast growth in ticket volumes. The councillor favoured renting over buying and suggested court locations closer to Cambridge and North Dumfries. Staff said rental options are being explored.
